answer_text:
Let \(\operatorname{ex}(n;P)\) denote the maximum number of edges in an \(n\)-vertex graph containing no copy of the Petersen graph \(P\) as a subgraph.

The key fact is the **Erdős–Stone–Simonovits theorem**: if \(H\) is a fixed graph with chromatic number \(\chi(H)=r\ge 3\), then

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{ex}(n;H)}{\binom{n}{2}}
=
1-\frac{1}{r-1}.
\]

So we only need the chromatic number of the Petersen graph.

1. The Petersen graph contains a 5-cycle, so it is not bipartite; hence \(\chi(P)\ge 3\).
2. The Petersen graph is 3-colorable, so \(\chi(P)=3\).

Applying the theorem with \(r=3\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{ex}(n;P)}{\binom{n}{2}}
=
1-\frac{1}{3-1}
=
1-\frac12
=
\frac12.
\]

Equivalently, \(\operatorname{ex}(n;P)=\frac{n^2}{4}+o(n^2)\), while \(\binom{n}{2}\sim \frac{n^2}{2}\).

\[
\boxed{\frac12}
\]
